reviews.review:
Incursion is a sci-fi roguelite shooter that takes a familiar survival formula and wraps it in a futuristic military setting centered on humanity’s struggle against relentless invaders. Developed and published by Rudel Studios, the game places players in the ranks of R.A.I.D., a defense force dedicated to stopping an ongoing alien threat. While the premise is straightforward, it serves as an effective backdrop for a gameplay experience built around constant combat, rapid progression, and repeated runs designed to test different strategies.

At its core, Incursion revolves around surviving overwhelming enemy assaults while steadily transforming a vulnerable recruit into a highly destructive combat specialist. The game embraces the addictive progression loop that has made the roguelite survival genre so popular. Every session rewards experimentation, encouraging players to adapt to new circumstances and build increasingly powerful combinations of abilities. The action remains fast and focused, ensuring that players spend more time fighting than navigating complicated systems or lengthy story sequences.

One of the game's most appealing features is its roster of six distinct classes. Each class introduces a different approach to combat, helping keep the experience fresh across multiple playthroughs. Whether players prefer aggressive offense, tactical positioning, or specialized ability-focused builds, the class system provides enough variation to make each run feel unique. This diversity adds meaningful replay value and helps prevent the repetitive feeling that can sometimes affect games within the genre.

The progression system is further strengthened by eighteen upgradeable abilities that can dramatically alter a run. These upgrades create a satisfying sense of growth as players unlock stronger attacks, enhanced survivability, and more effective crowd-clearing tools. The ability system rewards experimentation, allowing players to discover powerful synergies and tailor their builds to their preferred playstyle. Watching a modest character evolve into an unstoppable force against enormous enemy waves remains one of the game's most enjoyable aspects.

Incursion also benefits from its science-fiction identity. Rather than relying on traditional fantasy themes, the game embraces futuristic technology, advanced weaponry, and military-inspired aesthetics. This setting gives combat a distinct flavor and supports the game's emphasis on large-scale battles against hostile forces. The visual design may not be groundbreaking, but it effectively communicates the atmosphere of a desperate defense effort against an overwhelming extraterrestrial threat.

The inclusion of three different regions helps provide environmental variety throughout repeated runs. Although the number of locations is not extensive, the changing scenery helps break up the action and contributes to the overall replayability. Combined with the class system and upgrade combinations, these environments ensure that sessions remain engaging even after multiple attempts.

Where Incursion is likely to face the greatest challenge is in standing out from a crowded market. The roguelite survival genre has seen tremendous growth, and many competing titles offer similar progression systems and wave-based combat structures. Incursion does not attempt to radically reinvent the formula. Instead, it focuses on delivering a polished and enjoyable interpretation of established mechanics. Players searching for innovative genre-defining features may find the experience somewhat familiar, but those who enjoy the core gameplay loop of surviving enemy hordes and building increasingly powerful characters will likely find plenty to appreciate.

Overall, Incursion succeeds as a solid and entertaining action roguelite that understands exactly what its target audience wants. The combination of six classes, eighteen upgradeable abilities, multiple environments, and a futuristic military setting creates an enjoyable gameplay loop that encourages repeated experimentation. While it may not introduce revolutionary ideas, it delivers satisfying progression, accessible mechanics, and plenty of opportunities for players to refine their strategies across successive runs. Fans of survival shooters and roguelite progression systems should find Incursion to be a worthwhile addition to their library.

Rating: 6/10
